description:
pkix-path/src/lib.rs:1784, 2013, 2088, 2111, 2367

Multiple hot-path policy checks use `Vec::contains()` for OID lookups, which is O(n) per call. Specifically:

- `allowed_signature_algs` check (line 1784): `!allowed.contains(&cert.signature_algorithm.oid)` — called once per cert per chain walk
- `required_leaf_eku` check (line 2013): `!eku.0.iter().any(|e| e == req_oid)` — called for each required OID
- `mapped_policies` construction (line 2110): collected into Vec, then checked with `contains`
- Initial policy set filtering (line 2367): `!policy.initial_policy_set.contains(&tree[idx].valid_policy)`

For the common case (a handful of OIDs, short chains) this is practically negligible. However, the `allowed_signature_algs` field is documented as a slice of OIDs and is used in every cert in the chain. Since `ObjectIdentifier` implements `Hash`, callers could pass `&[ObjectIdentifier]` backed by a `HashSet`-sorted structure, OR the internal loop could build a `HashSet` once per chain walk rather than per cert.

This is a P3 style/performance note, not a correctness issue. A simpler approach: document that `allowed_signature_algs` is typically small (2–6 OIDs) and the O(n) cost is irrelevant in practice, and add a comment to that effect. Alternatively, the internal check could use a small stack-based linear search with an early exit.
notes: O(n) Vec::contains is negligible for typical 2-6 OID lists. Deferred as a micro-optimization. Comment added at allowed_signature_algs check.
title: Replace linear Vec contains() with HashSet for policy OID lookups in hot path
